Customer (Tidewater Medical) needs SOC2/ISO artifacts, SSO/SAML integration details, RBAC and audit log retention, and customer-managed KMS/HSM for PHI. transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-09-21 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~42 mins
- Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Cho (Redwood SE), Daniel Kim (Redwood CSM); Maya Torres (CISO, Tidewater), Ethan Blake (Head of Platform), Priya Sharma (DevOps), Omar Ruiz (Legal)

Auto-summary / Topics: SOC2/ISO status, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs & retention, encryption/KMS (customer-managed keys), Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs, data residency and egress concerns, next steps + artifact requests

[00:00] Samir (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. can you hear me ok?
[00:06] Maya (Tidewater): yep loud and clear, thanks.
[00:10] Samir (Redwood): quick intros, i'm samir ae, lena is our se, daniel cs. we're here to understand your security posture and requirements to see where redwood fits - hosted, dedicated, or private.
[00:22] Lena (Redwood): hi all. want to make sure we cover KMS, audit logs, sso, retention windows, and any regulatory constraints.
[00:30] Maya (Tidewater): great. high level, we're a med device software co handling PHI, so SOC2 is table stakes, ISO 27001 nice to have. we also need customer-managed keys for encryption at rest ideally, and strict retention controls.
[00:46] Ethan (Tidewater): also concerned about egress and data residency - some data needs to stay in us-east and not leave our VPC.
[00:54] Lena (Redwood): yup, understood. on redwood we offer three modes: hosted api (fastest), dedicated reserved capacity (dedicated gpus & network isolation in our infra), and private (vpc/on-prem). for PHI you can opt for dedicated or private with customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM and bring-your-own-key.
[01:12] Priya (Tidewater): when you say customer-managed KMS, is that BYOK where the keys live in our cloud KMS or do you host an HSM?
[01:18] Lena (Redwood): good q. we support both patterns - use your cloud KMS (aws/kms, gcp/kms) and we integrate via key wrapping, or for private deployments we can integrate with your HSM/FIPS module. sometimes we call it H-S-M but transcripts may show K-M-S, sorry, it's KMS/K G S, haha, minor transcription note.
[01:36] Maya (Tidewater): ok that's promising. next, RBAC - we need role separation, audit trails, SSO using SAML with Okta, and SCIM provisioning if possible.
[01:46] Samir (Redwood): we have SSO via SAML/OIDC, SCIM for user provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC. can ask lena to show RBAC model in the deep dive.
[01:56] Lena (Redwood): our RBAC supports per-route and per-model roles, token scoping, and admin/audit roles. audit logs capture request metadata, who called the API, the model id, tokens consumed, and the user identity if coming through SSO. retention windows are configurable for dedicated/private; hosted has default retention policy but enterprise add-on can extend retention and export logs to your cloud account.
[02:20] Omar (Tidewater): legal question - do you provide immutable audit logs and chain-of-custody? we need tamper-evidence for investigations.
[02:27] Lena (Redwood): we can ship audit logs to your S3 or cloud storage with immutability settings, or integrate with your SIEM via streaming. for private/on-prem you control retention and immutability. for hosted we offer append-only logs and signed log exports. we'll share how that looks in the docs.
[02:45] Ethan (Tidewater): what about SOC2 and pen tests? do you have a recent SOC2 Type II and third-party pen test?
[02:51] Samir (Redwood): yes, we have SOC2 Type II and an annual third-party penetration test; i'll share those artifacts after the call.
[02:59] Maya (Tidewater): will want the full scope and any exclusions. also are you ISO 27001 certified or in process?
[03:05] Samir (Redwood): currently SOC2 Type II, ISO roadmap - we can share status.
[03:10] Priya (Tidewater): retention: our compliance requires 7 years for some audit logs and 90 days for request payloads, is that doable?
[03:18] Lena (Redwood): for hosted our default is 30 days for request payloads, audit metadata 1 year, but with enterprise add-ons and dedicated/private you can extend to your retention windows, including pushing logs to your S3 and long-term retention. we'll confirm exact SLAs in the doc.
[03:34] Maya (Tidewater): also need to verify data deletion / right to be forgotten flows - can you purge customer data on demand and provide attestations?
[03:42] Lena (Redwood): yes - deletion APIs are available for private and dedicated; for hosted we have deletion flows and can provide deletion reports but timelines vary per plan. we'll include the deletion workflow in the follow-up.
[03:56] Ethan (Tidewater): network isolation - if we go dedicated, do we get VPC peering or private link? and can you guarantee no cross-tenant noisy neighbors?
[04:04] Lena (Redwood): dedicated includes tenant isolation at the infra layer; we offer VPC peering/privatelink for dedicated and private. for noisy neighbors we provide reserved capacity and can size pools to avoid cross-tenant interference; that's part of capacity planning.
[04:20] Maya (Tidewater): curious about model artifacts - do model weights ever persist in your storage? how do you manage KV cache?
[04:27] Lena (Redwood): model binaries are stored in our infra for hosted/dedicated; for private you can bring your own and we can run locally. KV cache is ephemeral in memory but can be cached across requests for performance; for compliance we can disable cross-request caching or ensure it resides on nodes dedicated to your tenant. we also support quantization but we'll document implications for deterministic logging.
[04:50] Priya (Tidewater): encryption in transit and at rest? TLS? FIPS?
[04:53] Lena (Redwood): TLS 1.2+/modern ciphers in transit. at rest encryption using AES-256; for FIPS/HSM we integrate in private deployments. if you need FIPS-compliant endpoints that's part of private/HSM integration.
[05:07] Omar (Tidewater): any certifications around supply chain or dependency scanning?
[05:12] Samir (Redwood): we do SCA and dependency scanning, and include that info in our security artifacts pack.
[05:18] Maya (Tidewater): what about subprocessor disclosures and data flow mapping? need that for our legal security review.
[05:24] Samir (Redwood): yes we maintain a subprocessors list and a data flow diagram; i'll include those links.
[05:30] Ethan (Tidewater): for latency sensitive workloads, do you recommend hosted with edge regions or dedicated pinned capacity?
[05:36] Lena (Redwood): for lowest latency and strict isolation, dedicated pinned pools in the region is best. hosted is fine for general workloads but dedicated gives predictability and private gives ultimate control and compliance.
[05:48] Maya (Tidewater): cost vs security tradeoff - we expect higher cost for dedicated/private but need to justify; please include pricing ranges in the SOW.
[05:56] Samir (Redwood): will do, include committed capacity pricing and options for burst, and pilot credits for evaluation.
[06:02] Priya (Tidewater): question about audit log format - is it JSON lines, what fields are included, can we get the raw payloads?
[06:09] Lena (Redwood): audit logs are JSON lines with timestamp, request id, model id, route, user identity, tokens consumed, and optionally redacted or full payloads depending on retention policy and redaction settings. we'll provide a sample schema and sample logs.
[06:26] Maya (Tidewater): how do you handle redaction for PII in logs?
[06:30] Lena (Redwood): we offer automatic PII redaction rules and manual redaction API; for PHI workloads we recommend turning on redaction and pushing full payloads to your own storage if you need to store raw content behind your own KMS.
[06:44] Ethan (Tidewater): ok. threat detection and alerting? integrate with our SIEM?
[06:49] Lena (Redwood): yes log streaming to SIEM, and we have alerting hooks for anomalous usage, spikes, and auth failures.
[06:58] Samir (Redwood): quick note - competitors like anthro or open ai call out similar features but our differentiation is unified ops and clear routing policies across hosted/dedicated/private.
[07:10] Omar (Tidewater): legal will review SOC2 and subprocessors. main ask is the evidence we can attach to our security review pack.
[07:18] Samir (Redwood): understood - will share SOC2 Type II, pen test summary, subprocessor list, data flow diagram, and RBAC docs.
[07:26] Maya (Tidewater): one more - can we get an architecture diagram for private deployment (on-prem)?
[07:31] Lena (Redwood): yes we'll include a reference on-prem architecture and network requirements.
[07:36] Priya (Tidewater): what are the SLAs for audit log export and retention?
[07:40] Lena (Redwood): we'll include SLA language - uptime SLA for dedicated, log delivery SLA for exports, and retention guarantees in the add-on.
[07:48] Ethan (Tidewater): curious about key rotation - if we use BYOK, what's the rotation model?
[07:53] Lena (Redwood): we support key rotation in your KMS and re-wrap keys periodically; for HSMs we can coordinate rotation windows.
[08:02] Samir (Redwood): ok looks like action items: samir shares artifacts; lena runs deep dive; tidewater provides compliance matrix and qps data. anything else?
[08:12] Maya (Tidewater): that'll cover it. legal may have follow-ups once they review docs.
[08:16] Samir (Redwood): perfect, we'll aim to get docs this week.

[35:00] Lena (Redwood): (later in call) to reiterate, for PHI we typically recommend dedicated or private, enable BYOK/HSM, push audit logs to your S3 and enable immutability, and use SAML + SCIM for provisioning.
[35:20] Ethan (Tidewater): sounds good. one more about backups - are backups encrypted with the same KMS keys?
[35:27] Lena (Redwood): yes backups are encrypted and can use your KMS in dedicated/private.
[36:05] Priya (Tidewater): can we run a short benchmark to validate latency and throughput before committing?
[36:10] Samir (Redwood): absolutely, we can set up a pilot and run a benchmark; lena will scope the test.
[36:18] Lena (Redwood): for the POC we'll need expected qps, model size, typical sequence lengths, and acceptable p95 latency.
[36:28] Ethan (Tidewater): i'll get that over.
[36:31] Samir (Redwood): ok final recap - next steps: samir share SOC2 + pen test + subprocessors + dataflow; lena schedule SE deep dive and benchmark plan; tidewater sends compliance template and qps/model info.
[36:45] Maya (Tidewater): thanks all, appreciate it.
[36:48] Omar (Tidewater): thanks.
[36:50] Samir (Redwood): thanks everyone, we'll follow up.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-attribution and small transcription errors (e.g., KMS spelled out, HSM heard as H-S-M). Some timestamps approximate.
